newsitem.title: MEXICO: Avantel announces flat-rate Mexico call charges.
newsitem.headline: Avantel announces flat-rate Mexico call charges.

text.p: Telephone company Avantel announced on Monday that its flat-rate call charges will apply to domestic long-distance and international markets when competition starts in 1997.

"About 40 percent of the long-distance market is residential. Avantel aims to capture a substantial part of that market over the coming years," the firm's advertising manager Jorge Rodriguez said at a news conference.
Avantel is a joint venture between MCI Communications Corp and Mexican bank Banamex.
Avantel will charge one and two pesos per minute for nighttime and daytime domestic long-distance calls, respectively, made from residential areas.
Daytime calls to the United States will cost five and seven pesos per minute, respectively, from the north and south of Mexico, and 3.5 and five pesos at night.
